arcs.line: {name} ({tag}) is in a room built for two and slept in by three, and has opinions.
{name} ({tag}) wrote home that the place looks like a postcard.
{name} ({tag}) has found the library, the refectory, and a radiator that works.
{name} ({tag}) has taken to eating at four o'clock, when the queue is shortest.
{name} ({tag}) sat on the floor of a lecture again, and says the acoustics are better down there.
{name} ({tag}) has put a bucket under the leak and named it.
{name} ({tag}) has changed their mind about their future twice this term, both times after a lecture.
{name} ({tag}) asked when the teaching starts and was given a pamphlet.
{name} ({tag}) has the same professor for three of four courses, and they are all Tuesday.
{name} ({tag}) is writing to the student paper about what the cuts have done to {school}.
{name} ({tag}) notes that the half-built thing outside their window has not moved since October.
{name} ({tag}) has met the interim CFO twice, which is twice more than they have met a dean.
{name} ({tag}) has won the essay prize, and is unbearable about it.
{name} ({tag}) is on academic probation and has promised to do better, in writing.
{name} ({tag}) has been seen reading another college's prospectus in the refectory.
{name} ({tag}) has joined three societies and founded a fourth.
{name} ({tag}) was first through the doors of the new building, and says it smells of paint.
{name} ({tag}) has done no work at all this week, but has done it on {quad}.
{name} ({tag}) came here to read {program}, which no longer exists, and has been reassigned.
{name} ({tag}) is in the first cohort to take the new courses in {program}.
{name} ({tag}) has been found asleep in the {school} building three nights running.
{name} ({tag}) is doing quite well, and has stopped writing home so often.
{name} ({tag}) has gone home. They did not say where they were going next.
{name} ({tag}) has withdrawn. The fees went up; the heating did not.
{name} ({tag}) has transferred to a college with a bigger library and a smaller reputation.
{name} ({tag}) graduates with the highest marks in {school} and a scholarship abroad.
{name} ({tag}) graduates; their thesis is being published, which nobody expected, least of all them.
{name} ({tag}) gives the commencement address and thanks a professor by name.
{name} ({tag}) graduates and has a post to go to in the autumn.
{name} ({tag}) graduates without fuss, which is how they did everything else.
{name} ({tag}) graduates, and has already asked when the reunions are.
{name} ({tag}) graduates with no plans and a forwarding address that will not last.
{name} ({tag}) graduates, and tells the photographer they would not do it again.
{name} ({tag}) graduates a term late, quietly, with nobody in the seats.
{name} ({tag}) has drawn up a rota for the bottom bunk, laminated it, and pinned it to the door.
{name} ({tag}) arrives at lectures twenty minutes early to get a seat, and now brings a book for the wait.
{name} ({tag}) wears a coat to seminars, indoors, and the tutor has stopped asking them to take it off.
{name} ({tag}) has been revising on {quad} since the first warm day, and has the sunburn to show for it.
{name} ({tag}) went to office hours to ask one question and stayed for two hours.
{name} ({tag}) has been taught {program} this term by a visitor, a doctoral student, and a very game professor from another department.
{name} ({tag}) is sharing one textbook with four others, and a timetable for who has it on Sundays.
{name} ({tag}) corrected a professor in a seminar, politely, and was right.
{name} ({tag}) has found a study group, and the study group has found a table in the corner that nobody else wants.
{name} ({tag}) has learned to cook one dish, and has cooked it for everyone on the corridor.
{name} ({tag}) has left to finish {program} somewhere it is still taught.
{name} ({tag}) has withdrawn; their parents read about the receivership in the paper before the college wrote.
{name} ({tag}) has gone home to help with the family business, and has promised to come back.
{name} ({tag}) has left after a second term on probation, and wrote a kind letter to their tutor on the way out.
{name} ({tag}) graduates first in a strong year, which in {school} this year took some doing.
{name} ({tag}) graduates with honours and is staying on to teach, at their tutor's quiet insistence.
{name} ({tag}) graduates with the top marks in {school} in a year when the college could not heat the exam hall.
{name} ({tag}) graduates with distinction, and the admissions office has already asked for a photograph for the prospectus.
{name} ({tag}) graduates, takes a job in town, and will be on the alumni committee within the decade.
{name} ({tag}) graduates and goes into schoolteaching, with every trick borrowed from one lecturer in particular.
{name} ({tag}) graduates on the second attempt at one paper and the first attempt at a job interview.
{name} ({tag}) graduates with a post in the city and a photograph on {quad} to prove the rest happened.
{name} ({tag}) graduates in {program}, which the college no longer teaches, and finds that employers have noticed.
{name} ({tag}) graduates into the same cuts that thinned their final year, with a degree and not much else yet.
{name} ({tag}) graduates without a reference, because nobody in {program} taught them long enough to write one.
{name} ({tag}) graduates and moves back into their childhood bedroom, to think.

readings.named: The handful of students the game follows through their four years: a lens on the cohorts, never a separate simulation.
readings.arc: What has happened to them, drawn from what was true of their class at the time.
readings.outcome: How they left: the class's own outcome distribution, one student's share of it.

lines.none: No named students yet. The game picks a handful out of each arriving class.
lines.introduced: The game will be following {names} of the {label}.
